In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

chronological age at en trance, amount of education, and occupational status are not good predictors of academic success, as measured by teachers1 marks, in a high school of the type represented by University High School, University or Min nesota, but that the occupational status of father does have some value in predicting academic success.
the results of this study do not indicate that chronological age at the time of entrance to elementary school has any value for predicting scholastic success as measured by marks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonintellectual factors studied are not of sufficient importance to warrant consideration for use in predicting school success.
the nonintellectual factors studied are not as useful for prediction purposes as are the intellectual factors, but that they are not without value.
